property_summary: After any series of calls ending with a Collect call, MinSum must be greater than zero if it was ever set via SetMinSum (since initialization must happen before SetMinSum can change MinSum).

When the contract is not yet initialized (intitalized is false), calling SetMinSum will revert, so MinSum remains 0; after initialization, SetMinSum succeeds, but if only SetMinSum is called before initialization, MinSum stays 0 and Collect reverts due to balance >= MinSum check failure.
After a Collect call that changes balance, MinSum must equal the value set by the last successful SetMinSum call after initialization.
After any sequence of calls ending with a successful Collect, the MinSum value is equal to the value set by the last SetMinSum call (if any) or remains 0 if SetMinSum was never called.
After calling Collect with a non-zero amount, the MinSum equals the value set by the last successful SetMinSum call (or 0 if never set).
After a call to Collect(uint256), the state variable MinSum remains unchanged from its initial value of 0.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, the value of MinSum equals the value set by the last successful SetMinSum call before Initialized was called.
After any sequence ending in Collect, MinSum equals the last value passed to the last SetMinSum before Initialized (or 0 if SetMinSum was never called).
After a call to Collect, MinSum is unchanged from the last value it had after the corresponding Put that increments the caller's balance (i.e., Collect does not modify MinSum).
After any sequence of calls ending with a call to Collect, the value of MinSum is unchanged from its value after the last SetMinSum call (if any) before Initialized was called.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, the value returned by c.SetLogFile() is not the zero address.
After any call to Collect(uint256) that does not revert, the value of c.LogFile() remains the same as before the call.
After any call to Collect(uint256), the value of c.SetLogFile() remains the same as before the call.
After any call to Collect, the address returned by c.LogFile() is the same as before the call.
After any call to Collect that returns true, the caller's balance in Acc is decremented by the collected amount.
The balance of the caller after Collect should decrease by the amount collected if the call succeeds.
After a successful Collect call, the LogFile contract's History length remains unchanged from before the call.
After any successful Collect call, the LogFile contract's History length should increase by exactly 1.
After a call to Collect(uint256), the History length of the LogFile contract should always increase by exactly 1 if the call succeeded and the conditions were met.
After any successful Collect call, the LogFile contract's address should be the same as the one set by SetLogFile.
The state variable 'intitalized' remains false after a Collect call regardless of the fuzz inputs.
After a Collect call, the contract is always initialized (intitalized is true) if MinSum was set to a positive value and the caller had sufficient balance.
When Collect is called with any amount, the initialized flag remains true (i.e., initialization is never undone).
After any Collect call, the contract's initialized flag is always true.
After Collect is called, the initialized flag is unchanged from its previous value.
The unlockTime after Put is at least the original unlockTime or block.timestamp plus _lockTime
After Collect call, the resulting unlockTime of the caller is always equal to the block.timestamp of the last Put call that updated it.

After a Collect call, the caller's unlockTime is never strictly greater than the block timestamp of that Collect call plus lockTime applied during a preceding Put call (i.e., unlockTime <= block.timestamp + _lockTime).
After a Collect call for the caller succeeds (does not revert), the caller's unlockTime equals the block.timestamp of the last Put call that could have updated it.
After a call to Collect from an address, the caller's unlockTime is always exactly equal to the block.timestamp when Put was called plus the _lockTime specified in that Put call.
After a Collect call with amount less than the caller's balance, the caller's balance should decrease by the collected amount.
The total number of Log entries increases by exactly one after each successful Collect call.
After a Collect call, the caller's balance in the contract is either unchanged or decreased by the exact amount requested, depending on whether the collect succeeds.
After Collect, the balance of the caller in the Log contract (History length, or LastMsg) reflects the Put call's data (specifically the value transferred in the last Put before Collect).
After a Collect call, the contract's total balance (sum of all Acc balances plus the contract's ether) is invariant modulo the transferred amount.
Collect only succeeds when caller's balance is at least MinSum and withdrawal amount and current time exceeds unlock time, and balance decreases by exactly the withdrawn amount.
After a Collect call, the caller's balance (in Acc) plus the amount collected equals the balance before the call.
After a Collect call, the caller's balance in Acc does not increase relative to before the call.
After a Collect call, the sum of caller's balance in Acc and the contract's ether balance cannot exceed what would be expected from deposits only.
After a Collect call, the caller's balance in Acc is not less than zero.
After a Collect call, the unlockTime of the caller is never decreased from its previous value.
After a Collect call preceded by a Put call, the unlockTime of the caller is at least the sum of the current block timestamp and the lock time specified in the most recent Put call.
After a Collect call, the unlockTime of the caller is always at least the block.timestamp at the time of the previous Put call plus the lockTime of that Put call.

After a Collect call, the unlockTime of the caller is never less than the block.timestamp at the time of the most recent Put call plus the lockTime of that Put call, when the Put call increased the unlockTime.
After a Collect call that succeeds, the unlockTime of the caller is strictly greater than the previous unlockTime (i.e., it is increased).
The Collect function should only succeed (not revert) when the caller's balance is sufficient and the current time is strictly greater than the unlock time, not greater or equal.
After Collect succeeds (returns without revert), the caller's balance must decrease by exactly the collected amount when the unlock time has strictly passed.
After Collect, the caller's balance decreases only when block.timestamp is strictly greater than unlockTime, not when it's equal.
After a successful Collect call, the caller's balance decreases by the collected amount only when block.timestamp is strictly greater than unlockTime.
The Collect function should only decrease the caller's balance when block.timestamp is strictly greater than acc.unlockTime, not when it is equal.
After a successful Collect call, the balance of msg.sender must decrease by exactly the amount withdrawn (_am).
After a successful Collect call, the caller's balance in the contract decreases by at most the withdrawn amount.
After a successful Collect call, the balance of the caller in the contract decreases by at most _am.
After a successful Collect call, the caller's balance in the contract decreases by at most the withdrawn amount plus 1.
After a successful Collect call, the caller's balance in the contract decreases by exactly the amount withdrawn (_am).
After calling Collect(uint), the value logged to the Log contract must equal the amount actually transferred.
The amount recorded in the Log after a successful Collect must be the same as the amount transferred to msg.sender.
After a successful Collect call, the value stored in the last log message must equal the amount requested.
After Collect(uint _am) succeeds, the amount parameter recorded in the Log contract must equal the requested _am.
The value logged by Collect(_am) must equal the value successfully withdrawn by the user.
